trp_cage.headline: The smallest thing that folds
trp_cage.note: Twenty residues, and one of the fastest folders known. A single short helix packs against a proline-rich tail to bury one tryptophan. There is almost nothing here but the arpeggio and one late cadence - listen for how little the piece needs to say.

villin_hp36.headline: Three helices, microseconds
villin_hp36.note: The villin headpiece subdomain: 36 residues, three helices, and a folding time measured in microseconds. Almost all pad and no rhythm, because there is no sheet in it at all.

ww_domain.headline: All sheet, no helix
ww_domain.note: Three antiparallel strands and nothing else. The staccato figure carries the whole piece and the pad never enters - the clearest demonstration that the voices really are reading secondary structure.

protein_g_b1.headline: Both voices at once
protein_g_b1.note: One helix lying across a four-stranded sheet, in 56 residues. Pad and staccato figure together, which is what an alpha-beta protein sounds like.

ubiquitin.headline: The beta-grasp
ubiquitin.note: Seventy-six residues wrapping a mixed sheet around one helix. Listen for the long-range contacts low in the register as the two halves of the chain find each other.

alpha3d.headline: Designed, not evolved
alpha3d.note: A de novo three-helix bundle - a protein somebody drew rather than found. It folds cleanly because it was designed to, and the piece is correspondingly tidy.

proinsulin.headline: A disordered middle
proinsulin.note: The A and B chains are confident; the C-peptide joining them is not, and is cut out during maturation. Mean confidence sits near 55, so the whole piece stays somewhat out of tune - the connecting peptide is the reason.

lysozyme.headline: A core pinned by disulfides
lysozyme.note: Hen egg white lysozyme: 129 residues, mostly helical with a small sheet, and four disulfide bonds holding the core together. High confidence throughout, so it is the brightest and most in-tune of the set.

alpha_synuclein.headline: It never resolves - and that is correct
alpha_synuclein.note: Intrinsically disordered: in isolation it has no fixed structure to find. Confidence stays near 35 from beginning to end, so the piece is a detuned wash that never cadences. This is the one to play to hear what a bad prediction sounds like - except that here the prediction is right, and the protein really is like this.

myoglobin.headline: Eight helices, no sheet
myoglobin.note: The globin fold: 153 residues in eight helices around a haem pocket. Sustained pad almost throughout, and a late cadence as the bundle closes.

gfp.headline: A barrel the model did not find
gfp.note: Green fluorescent protein is an eleven-stranded beta barrel with a helix threaded down its axis. This trajectory does not get there: mean confidence is 34, and it never resolves. Worth hearing next to lysozyme, which does.

beta2ar_7tm.headline: Seven helices across a membrane
beta2ar_7tm.note: The transmembrane bundle of the beta-2 adrenergic receptor: 314 residues, seven long helices. The largest thing in the gallery, and the pad has the most to hold.

genie2_76aa_seed1.headline: A protein that has never existed
genie2_76aa_seed1.note: Not a prediction and not a simulation: a backbone sampled from noise by a diffusion model. There is nothing to converge on, so it never cadences - what the confidence tracks here is how far along the denoising is, not how right anything is.
